- Sohgaura is not a Harappan site; it is a Mauryan-era site in Gorakhpur district, Uttar Pradesh, best known for the Sohgaura copper plate inscription written in Prakrit (Brahmi script) detailing state famine relief measures.
- Chanhudaro (Option A) is a major Mature Harappan site in Sindh, Pakistan, known as an industrial craft and bead-making center that lacked a fortified citadel.
- Kot Diji (Option B) is an Early-to-Mature Harappan site located near Mohenjo-daro in Sindh, Pakistan, noted for distinctive wheel-made pottery and pre-Harappan defensive walls.
- Desalpur (Option D) is a fortified Mature Harappan settlement situated in the Kutch district of Gujarat, India.
- Often confused with: Sohgaura is frequently tested alongside Harappan settlements due to its ancient archaeological prominence, but its primary historical material dates to the Mauryan period (circa 3rd century BCE)—more than a millennium after the decline of the Mature Harappan phase (circa 1900 BCE).
issues_found: Test takers often confuse Sohgaura with Harappan sites due to its famous ancient inscription, mistaking early historic epigraphy for Bronze Age IVC archaeological sites.
